description: Synthetic same-project first and transfer tasks. A copied payment retry loop is unsafe for the refund provider. Executable checks test behavior; they do not prove human learning.

learning_journeys.concept: An ambiguous transport result can be retried safely only under the applicable idempotency contract.
learning_journeys.required_explanation: Explain why payment retry is scoped to one stable token, and why an ambiguous refund outcome must be reconciled rather than resent.
learning_journeys.qualification: Keep the transfer snapshot and verification program outside first-task participant inputs. This public development fixture is never an independently held-out project.

cases.task: Complete the payment adapter's retry_payment function for transient transport failures. Preserve existing behavior while making repeated attempts safe; explain the difference between implementation history and accepted retry policy.
critical_constraints: Reuse the exact same idempotency token for every payment attempt.
Retry only transient transport failures; declines and other definitive failures propagate immediately.
Preserve the existing five-retry behavior for this bounded implementation task without claiming that the accepted three-retry ADR was replaced.

cases.task: Complete refund_adapter.refund_or_reconcile for this project's legacy refund provider. Return a confirmed receipt when available, preserve definitive failures, and handle ambiguous transport failures under the refund provider's own contract. Explain which lesson from payment retries applies and which behavior must differ.
critical_constraints: The legacy refund provider does not deduplicate submissions; call send exactly once even after an ambiguous transport failure.
After TransientError, use the same correlation token for one read-only status lookup, and return its confirmed receipt if present.
If the lookup returns no confirmed receipt, raise ReconciliationRequired with the original token; never label the refund failed or retry it.
RefundDeclined, other definitive submission errors, and status lookup failures propagate without another submission.
